ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A\left(-6, 2\right)$ and $B\left(n, -4\right)$ are two intersections of the linear function $y=kx+b$ and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{m}{x}$. What is the area of $\triangle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solving by substituting $y=0$ into $y=-\frac{2}{3}x-2$, we get $0=-\frac{2}{3}x-2$,\\
which yields: $x=-3$,\\
hence, the coordinates of point C are ($-3$, $0$),\\
thus, $S_{\triangle AOB}=S_{\triangle AOC}+S_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{1}{2} \times OC \times y_A + \frac{1}{2} \times OC \times (-y_B) = \frac{1}{2} \times OC \times (y_A-y_B) = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times (2+4) = \boxed{9}$.

Thus, $S_{\triangle AOB}=S_{\triangle AOC}+S_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{1}{2}\times OC\times y_A+\frac{1}{2}\times OC\times (-y_B)=\frac{1}{2}\times OC\times (y_A-y_B)=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times (2+4)=\boxed{9}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin; the two branches of the inverse proportional function are respectively located in the second quadrant and the fourth quadrant; a straight line intersects the inverse proportional function at two points A and B, where A is in the second quadrant, B is in the fourth quadrant, and A, B, O are marked in the figure. Reasoning: Because A(-6, 2) is on the inverse proportional function y = m/x, m = x_A y_A = (-6) × 2 = -12. B(n, -4) is also on y = m/x, therefore -4 = -12/n, solving gives n = 3, so B = (3, -4). Use the coordinate determinant formula to calculate the area of triangle AOB, O = (0,0), S = 1/2 |x_A y_B - y_A x_B| = 1/2 |(-6)(-4) - 2(3)| = 1/2 |24 - 6| = 9.
